[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Sum of Mutated Array Closest to Target** [LC 1300 · Sum of Mutated Array Closest to Target](https://leetcode.com/problems/sum-of-mutated-array-closest-to-target/){difficulty="Medium"}

The answer is a **value**, not an index, and it lies in $[0, \max(\mathit{arr})]$: a cap above the maximum changes nothing, so it ties with $\max(\mathit{arr})$ and loses the tie; a negative cap only moves the sum further below a positive target. Over that range, $S(v) = \sum_i \min(a_i, v)$ is **non-decreasing** (raising the cap never lowers any element) and **piecewise linear**: it rises by the number of elements above $v$ per unit step and bends only at the array's own values. "Closest to target" on a non-decreasing function is a search for the *crossing*: the first cap $v$ with $S(v) \ge \mathit{target}$ and the cap $v - 1$ just below it are the only contenders, and the tie rule picks the smaller. So binary search the flip of $P(v)$: "$S(v) \ge \mathit{target}$" over a range of *values*, then compare the two caps at the seam.

[Solved in full in @sec-bst-p4-b.]{.card-link}
